_comment: The single source of truth for what every Cinema client says when it cannot
reach the server. Consumed by four test suites so the copy cannot drift:
crates/plurxd/src/http/web.rs        (the shipped classifier carries every class)
Adding a class here fails all four until every client implements it. That is
the point: a taxonomy one client silently lacks is not a taxonomy.
See docs/CLIENT-CONNECTIVITY.md for how each platform maps its native errors

offline.meaning: This device has no network at all. Nothing was sent.
offline.title: You're offline
offline.detail: This device isn't connected to a network.

unreachable.meaning: The network is up but the server did not accept the connection: refused, host down, or no route.
unreachable.title: Can't reach {server}
unreachable.detail: The network is working, but the server didn't answer. It may be powered off, restarting, or on another network.

unknown_host.meaning: The address does not resolve. DNS failure, or a name that no longer exists on this network.
unknown_host.title: Can't find {server}
unknown_host.detail: Nothing on this network answers to that address. If the server moved, point Cinema at its new one.

timeout.meaning: The connection was made or attempted, but no answer arrived before the deadline.
timeout.title: No answer from {server}
timeout.detail: The server accepted the connection but didn't answer in time. It may be busy or still starting up.

insecure.meaning: TLS failed: certificate untrusted, expired, or hostname mismatch. Never retried silently.
insecure.title: Couldn't connect securely to {server}
insecure.detail: The secure connection failed. The server's certificate may have changed or expired.

server_error.meaning: The server was reached and answered, but with 5xx or a body the client cannot use.
server_error.title: Error from {server}
server_error.detail: The server answered with an error. Nothing is wrong with this device or your network.

unknown.meaning: The fallback. Anything the classifier cannot place lands here rather than leaking a native error string.
unknown.title: Something went wrong

rules.no_raw_transport_text: No class may render a platform error string (URLError.localizedDescription, Throwable.message, TypeError.message) to the user. Native text goes to diagnostics only.
rules.signin_is_not_credentials: A transport failure during sign-in must render its connectivity class, never a credentials message. Only HTTP 401/403 means the password was wrong, and then every client says credentials_message verbatim.
rules.every_error_offers_retry: Every class carries at least the retry action, and every surface that renders a class must expose it.
rules.cached_content_wins: A failed refresh over content already on screen shows a transient short-form notice; it must not replace the content with an error state.
